fieldMarks: Male: all glossy black with whitish eyes; female dull gray-brown with dark eyes
Shorter-tailed than Common Grackle and a bit larger than Brown-headed Cowbird
behavior: Walks on the ground searching for food, sometimes wading or catching insects in flight; may follow farm machinery
Usually forages in flocks except when nesting
Insects (grasshoppers, crickets, beetles), seeds, waste grain and berries
habitat: Open and semi-open country: fields, prairies, farms, parks, shrubby areas near water; often around human habitations including suburban lawns and parking lots.
range: Breeds from central interior British Columbia to the western Great Lakes, south to northwestern Baja California, Nevada, Texas and northern Iowa; present year-round in parts of the western U.S. and winters east to the southeastern U.S. and Mexico.

lookalikes.name: Rusty blackbird
lookalikes.howToTell: Rusty is less glossy with a thinner bill, yellow eyes and, in fall, rusty feather edges.
